title: SRE operational playbook: weekly reliability sync prep
content:
Purpose:
- Quick prep notes for the weekly SRE ops + reliability review (30–45m). Keep this as my crib sheet during the sync and for post-meeting capture.

Agenda (30m):
- 0–5m: Quick wins & blockers (round robin)
- 5–12m: SLO health snapshot + trends (latency P50/P95, availability, error budget burn rates)
- 12–22m: Paging trends & hot signals (what paged us this week, where to focus)
- 22–32m: Top 3 incidents recap (status, mitigations, owners)
- 32–38m: Open action items follow-up (blockers, owners, due dates)
- 38–45m: Canary/rollout risk review + any escalations needed

Quick SLO snapshot (last 7d / 30d):
- Host API availability SLO (99.95%)
  - 7d: 99.92% (0.03% under target -> small burn, mostly during 2026-06-26 outage window)
  - 30d: 99.96% (on target)
- Latency (text-generation endpoint) P95 target: 350ms
  - 7d: P95 = 410ms (spike on 6/26 during incident, median steady at ~180ms)
  - Kill points: watch large batch jobs around 02:00 UTC that push queue depth
- Embeddings availability SLO (99.9%)
  - 7d: 99.88% (paging twice this week -> follow-up below)
- Error budget burn rates (7d):
  - Hosted API: 1.4x baseline (concerning, but concentrated to two events)
  - Dedicated customers: 0.3x (healthy)

Paging trends (last 14 days):
- Total pages: 27 (avg ~1.9/day) up from 12 prior period- Top 3 page sources:
  1) Kernel OOMs on warmup nodes (INC-3421) — 9 pages 
     - Pattern: OOMs when model cache warms simultaneously after autoscale events.
     - Immediate mitigation: reduce warmup parallelism (deployed 6/28, monitoring).
  2) High tail latency from batching overload (INC-3478) — 7 pages
     - Triggered by periodic large-ttl batch jobs from internal experiments.
     - Short-term: apply backpressure on the batcher for experiment namespace.
  3) Tokenization failure rate spike (transcoding microservice) — 5 pages
     - Root cause: new model tokenizer changes, regressions in tokenizer lib.
     - Plan: pin tokenizer lib for production models until PR validated.

Top incidents (summary and next steps):
- Incident A: "Warmup OOM storm" (INC-3421) — 6/26
  - Impact: ~12m regional availability drop for text-gen, ~0.04% SLO loss for the day.
  - Root cause: concurrency + model cache eviction thrash during autoscale.
  - Work done: reduced max warmup concurrency, added staggered warmup schedule, improved memory headroom alerting.
  - Follow-ups: (1) refine kernel memory accounting (Samir, due 2026-07-08), (2) run chaos-replay to validate warmup settings (Luis, due 2026-07-12).
- Incident B: "Batch queue overload" (INC-3478) — 6/29
  - Impact: sustained P95 increase for 30–90m in US region; generated multiple pages.
  - Root cause: large experimental job exceeded soft-limits; batcher lacked per-namespace limits.
  - Work done: emergency throttle, temporarily blocklisted experiment customer, rolled out per-namespace throttle PR.
  - Follow-ups: (1) add long-tail latency telemetry to alerting (Maya, due 2026-07-05), (2) policy to require heavy-experiment opt-in with quotas (PM-129, product).
- Incident C: "Tokenizer regressions" — intermittent
  - Impact: ~5–8% spike in tokenization errors for certain model variants; caused retries and some page noise.
  - Root cause: upstream tokenizer lib change + missing test coverage for edge-case scripts.
  - Work done: rolled back tokenizer lib for prod; added unit tests for corner cases.
  - Follow-ups: (1) integrate tokenizer fuzz tests into CI (Jenna, due 2026-07-09), (2) create rapid rollback runbook for tokenizer changes (Maya, due 2026-07-03).

Open action items (captured here for assigned owners):
- Samir: kernel memory accounting spec and perf impact analysis — due 2026-07-08
- Luis: chaos-replay run validating staggered warmup — due 2026-07-12
- Maya: add long-tail latency metrics to alerting (dashboard + alert thresholds) — due 2026-07-05
- Jenna: CI tokenizer fuzz tests + runbook doc — due 2026-07-09
- Product / PM: finalize heavy-experiment opt-in + quota policy (link PM-129) — due 2026-07-15
- Oncall rotations: confirm July oncall swaps (I have action to confirm with ops-calendar) — due 2026-07-02

Canary / rollout notes:
- Upcoming: model-quantization rollout for v2-small next week; risk: memory regressions and slower small-batch P50.
  - Prechecks: run 50-connection canary for 2h per region, validate memory headroom metrics and P95 latency.
  - If P95 > 1.2x baseline or memory headroom drops below 15%, abort and rollback.
  - Owner for canary monitoring: Luis (live watch) + Pager duty: Samir on-call window.

Escalations & quick contacts:
- Pager escalation chain: Samir Rao -> Maya Chen -> Head SRE (Priya Kapoor)
- Platform eng on-call for infra (kernel / nodes): Luis Ortega
- Product escalation (policy or contract risk): Jenna Park

Notes to self (prep prompts for meeting):
- Push fast on the long-tail metric: convince infra to add p99.9 percentile for batch queue time (shows queuing pressure).
- Ask PM about experiment gating: do we want hard throttles or soft quota + billing?
- Clarify SLO math: confirm how 7d burn projects into 30d budget for hosted API (numbers look fine but want explicit confirmation).
- Bring up need for more synthetic checks that mimic large-batch traffic (we have token-level checks but not batch-scheduling checks).

Post-meeting capture template (copy into meeting notes):
- Decision / Summary: 
- New Action Items (owner / due): 
- Follow-ups escalated to product / platform: 
- Next check-in: date/time

Random scratchpoints (for later):
- Consider a small "grace period" config for warmup that delays eviction for N minutes after autoscale events.
- Evaluate switching to a different tokenizer lib for rare edge cases if fuzzing shows endemic failures.
- Revisit alert noise: drop low-value tokenization pages from paging path, move to paged dashboard instead.

-- end of prep notes --
